note: Ratchet for `scripts/loc-metrics.py`. Every number below is lines of git-tracked source, classified by the lexer in `scripts/lib/loc_classify.py`. They may only go DOWN — raising a limit to make a build green defeats the point of measuring, so a rise fails the gate. When a rise is deliberate, run `scripts/loc-metrics.py --baseline` and commit the new file in the SAME commit that grew the tree. Generated files (`@generated` / `DO NOT EDIT` in the header) are measured but excluded from these limits, because appending a wire kind must never fail a size gate. The `*.comment` numbers are measured and diffed but NOT gated: a gate that makes deleting documentation the cheapest way to go green is pointed at the wrong thing. What these limits do NOT cover, stated so the total has a denominator: the programme's own tooling, 11 `.py` files (3,434 code lines) and 25 `.sh` files (3,821), 7,255 code lines in all -- roughly 4.4% of the tree, and rising, because this tooling is inside its own blind spot. Counting them needs a `#`-comment lexer for two more languages, here-documents and docstrings included, and until that exists moving logic into a script still reads as reduction.
measured:
2026-08-10 on branch `feat/cross-folia-region-commit-#179` (base ee6d61f), by `scripts/loc-metrics.py --baseline`. Read this field before assuming a rise was lazy.

The rise is +449 java.main.code, +445 java.test.code and +3 kotlin.main.code, and all of it is server task 4 deliverable 6 -- the cross-Folia-region commit path (issue #179, L-64). Five new production classes in `endpoints/paper-plugin` (`NoderaFoliaRegionMap`, `FoliaOwnershipProbe`, `CrossRegionCommit`, `CrossRegionRefusedException`, `TransferStoreJournal`), the enable-time wiring and the live ALIGN-1 gate self-check in `NoderaEndpointPlugin`, three new suites (`NoderaFoliaRegionMapTest`, `CrossRegionCommitTest`, `CrossFoliaRegionCommitIT`, 15 tests) and three new checks in `FoliaScenario` F1. The Kotlin lines are three `testImplementation` entries in that module's build script.

This is new capability, not duplicated capability: the engine primitives it drives -- `EntityTransferCoordinator`, `JointTransferApprover`, `EntityTransferCertificate`, `TransferStore` -- already existed and had zero production call sites, and nothing was forked to reach them. Five methods that turned out to have no caller at all were deleted rather than stamped; the reasoning is in `fixtures/structure/budget.json`. The test half is nearly as large as the production half by design: `CrossFoliaRegionCommitIT` builds two real region threads, a third commit thread and two distinct one-sided-failure injections, because the row's exit clause is about what does NOT happen on the failure paths.

Every bucket sits exactly on its measured value, because that is what `--baseline` writes; there is never any headroom, so a one-line fix and its test cost a stamp. That pressure is the known cost of an exact ratchet, and the answer to it is a reason recorded here, not a limit with slack in it. The pre-#179 narrative for this file (the PR #222 reduction wave, and why the like-for-like delta there was -9,461 rather than +4,253) is preserved in `git log -p scripts/lib/loc-baseline.json`.
